chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ja'far ibn Muhammad ibn Abi al-Subbah, from his father, from his grandfather, who said:

I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): A youth befriended a maid, so she handed over to him four thousand dirhams. Then she said to him: 'If there is a spoiling (of relationship) between me and you, return these four thousand to me.' So the youth worked with it and profited. Then the youth got married and intended to repent. How should he deal with it?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'He should return the four thousand dirhams to her, and the profit is for him.'

key_terms.صَادَقَتْهُ: She gave him a sum of money as a trust/friendship gift

ai.seo_question: Who keeps the profit from money held in trust if the trust is returned?
ai.summary: Recorded in al-Kafi, this hadith clarifies the distinction between the principal (asl) and profit (ribh) in a conditional trust, ruling that the woman retains her original four thousand dirhams while the young man keeps the earnings, reflecting the principle that risk and effort belong to the user. This ruling is significant in Shia jurisprudence for distinguishing between simple deposit (amanah) and profit-sharing arrangements, ensuring fairness when the underlying relationship dissolves. It underscores the ethical imperative of returning the specific entrusted amount while acknowledging the user's right to the fruits of their labor.
